Sun.Desc:
The Sun is a big ball of super heated
plazma that is supported by pressure
via Nuclear fusion. Or at least thats our
current understanding. Its surface
temperature is about 5527°C or 9980°F
which means that almost all of the light it
gives off is from blackbody radiative heat.

This common misconception is that a light
particle starts at the core of the sun
and works its wayoutward for thousands
of years until it reaches the surface,
while true that some photons do this,
basically 100% that we see are made 
directly on the surface from the glow of
the high temperature.

Earth.Desc:
Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
This planet is where every human has 
grown up and is the only planet we know of 
that we can live on.

It contains a breathable atmosphere
composed of 21% Oxygen and 78% Nitrogen,
along with ~1% of other gases.

Being where we are from its orbit is the 
easiest to get to and therefore it has
the highest density of orbiting objects
and satellites in the solar system. At the
same time,it is the most diverse, with
vast oceans anddeep forests, that it turns
out we have mapped more of the surfaces
of the Moon and Mars than we have of
our own planet.

Moon.Desc:
The moon is Earth's moon, or in other 
words, Earth's only natural satellite.
It is the same moon that every person
has seen when they look up at the 
night sky.

It is also true that we only ever get
to see one side of the Moon,
because it is tidally locked. Like almost
every other moon in the solar system,
gravity has a stronger pull on one side
and keeps that side naturally facing us.
As you explore more, you will see that
there is not one moon depicted here that
is not tidally locked. While intuitivley
it seems like this phenomenon is rare,
it is actually very common.

Mercury.Desc:
Mercury is the first planet from the Sun
and it is the second hottest. It does not
have any atmosphere because it is the
closest to the Sun, meaning its too hot
and gravity too weak to support it. 

Fun fact: while Venus is known for having
a day longer than its year, in terms of
actually living on the surface, Mercury's
day to year ratio is actually longer;
Because Mercury spins in the same direction
the rotation is closer to matching,(while
NOT tidally locked) it takes longer than
one Mercury year for the sun to pass over
the surface once. This works out to
2 Mercury years per Mercury day due to its
3:2 rotation to orbital ratio.

Venus.Desc:
Venus is the Second Planet from the Sun
and is the second largest rocky planet
in the Solar System. It has a very harsh
atmosphere, with ~90x the pressure as
Earth, full of 96% Carbon Dioxide and
temperatures on average of 467°C
or 872°F, you would not survive for
a second here.

Dont even think about wanting to come
visit because this place would destroy any
vehicle meant to keep you alive.

Venus is also the brightest planet as
seen from Earth and can usually be
spotted early mornings before Sunrise
or just after Sunset.

Mars.Desc:
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun
and is the second most "habitable" planet
in the solar system besides Earth. Don't
Let this fool you though, you would die
in less than a minute trying to breathe
its air.

Mars's atmosphere is much thinner than
Earth's, 95% Carbon dioxide with only
0.6% of Earth's pressure. Because of this
parachutes don't work completely and
spacecraft need rockets to touch down on
the surface. People would need a spacesuit
to walk outside.

Due to the lower protection from the
atmosphere and the lack of magnetic field,
Mars is much more prone to radiation,
so anyone living on Mars would need good
radiation shielding. Fluids like water seem
to do a good job at blocking damaging
radiation so the technology exists its only
a matter of infrastructure.

Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos,
if you're even willing to call them moons.
They are both very small and believed to
be captured asteroids. both are only a
couple dozen miles/kilometers wide. They
both travel opposite directions from the
perspective of the surface, Phobos East,
and Deimos slower
west.

It is the only other rocky planet than
Earth to have moons.
